research_updates.title: Boundary audit — original 119.5 acres separated from 25 current Vitesse accounts
research_updates.notes: City Ordinance 1182 identifies original map-tax-lot 1515000000311, 119.5 acres, and a three-parcel partition. On 2026-09-06 the public Assessor portal https://pso.crookcountyor.gov/pso was queried by Name=VITESSE across result pages 1-3; it returned 25 current accounts, four personal and 21 real, under VITESSE LLC or META PLATFORMS INC DBA VITESSE LLC, spanning nine displayed map-tax-lot strings. Exact-address account 19380 resolves 735 SW Connect Way to 151501-00-01102 and legal description PP 2010-04 PARCEL 2; related accounts 19271 and 19923 share that tax lot at 511 SW Connect Way. The broader owner result also includes 500 Connect Way, Social Loop, Connect Loop, Houston Lake Road and undetermined/remote holdings, so it is not treated as a campus parcel set. The official deed index at https://clerk.crookcountyor.gov/DigitalResearchRoomPublic/Disclaimer was accessed; County instructions permit only party-name search, not address/map/account/legal-description search, and bot verification blocked an anonymous Vitesse query, while document images are paid. No deed image or current legal-description crosswalk was inferred.

research_updates.title: Investment audit — three LRZ facility proposals added without relabeling as spend
research_updates.notes: Business Oregon resource re77-krua was queried directly at https://data.oregon.gov/resource/re77-krua.json for certified_business_firm='Vitesse LLC (Facebook)' and DC No. 1, 2 and 3. Proposed investment is $188,168,000, $201,000,000 and $260,175,000, with required minima of $10,450,000, $200,000,000 and $200,000,000; those proposals are retained separately from the approximate $210.4 million through-2011 reported capital cost, the 2018 $750 million expansion forecast and the 2021 greater-than-$2 billion campus-at-completion forecast. Planning, assessor, permit, contractor and operator searches using Facebook, Meta, Vitesse, PRN1-6, capital cost, investment, equipment and assessed/exempt value did not produce an audited annual expenditure ledger, equipment/construction split, current realized cumulative capital or a nonoverlapping phase reconciliation.

source.title: City of Prineville letter on Facebook Prineville Data Center Project
source.notes: Mayor-authored legislative record summarizing an ECONorthwest analysis for January 2010 through December 2011. research_updates.title: Construction and procurement audit — exact ePermitting record added; ledger remains unreconciled
research_updates.notes: Crook County directs permit-history users to Oregon ePermitting at https://aca-oregon.accela.com/oregon/Cap/CapHome.aspx?module=Building&TabName=Building. Anonymous Building search used 01/01/2009-09/06/2026, street 735, fragment Con and city Prineville and returned 100+ records. Exact record 217-26-000826-STR is Permit Issued for Meta Prineville Fiber Huts / Vitesse, 138 / Fiber hut 07, owned by Vitesse, with Fortis Construction Inc. as applicant/licensed professional and a $140,029.33 job value; it is retained as one permit valuation. Exact-address results also showed electrical, mechanical, fire-revision and void records, demonstrating overlap. Searches of City packets, DPR, Fortis, Rosendin, Mortenson, OSHA and supplier pages using Facebook, Meta, Vitesse, PRN1-6, permit, generator, contractor, subcontractor, supplier, payroll and local spend found identities and scopes but no downloadable all-record ledger, reconciled nonoverlapping construction value, worker hours, job-years, invoices, supplier geography or local-spend share.

source.notes: Operator release states that the first custom-built Prineville data center opened in 2011, two additional buildings had been announced to bring total campus footprint above 3.2 million square feet, the additional investment was $750 million, 100 new jobs were expected, and operations already supported 350 jobs in the region. research_updates.title: Fiscal and incentive audit — annual abatements, facility values, bills and fee schedules separated
research_updates.notes: Business Oregon resource re77-krua and its 2016-2025 attached composite reports now support ten published Crook County Facebook/Meta potential-additional-tax observations and three facility-level 2024 exempt assessed values: $927,721,260, $571,612,240 and $4,526,256,370. Crook County top-taxpayer PDFs report Vitesse taxable assessed value/tax amount of $10,478,100/$165,478.53 for 2024-25 and $10,314,110/$182,293.11 for 2025-26; these are bills, not payment proof. Assessor account 19380 contributes a separate 2016-2025 exempt-account value history. City Resolutions 1117, 1271 and 1329 establish the three approvals; Resolution 1393 Exhibit A schedules annual project fees of $110,000, $190,000 and amended $750,000 for PRN1-3, PRN4 and PRN5-6. City/County allocation tables mix Facebook, Apple and future estimates, so they are not receipts. The City budget/ACFR, County budget, treasurer payment portal, DOR tax-expenditure/corporate-statistics pages, OIA program page and 2024 DOR central assessment roll were searched using Vitesse/Facebook/Meta, LRZ, PILOT, project fee, payment, distribution and 735 SW Connect Way; the DOR address hit was Zayo centrally assessed telecom property and was excluded. Project-specific SDC and franchise records remain, but no Meta-only cash-payment dates, recipient distributions, account-to-facility crosswalk, compliance certificates, OIA benefit or same-scope public-service cost was published.

research_updates.title: Utility, water and environmental audit — exact dockets and portals documented; water conversion retained
research_updates.notes: OPUC UM 1989 Order 19-238 records Vitesse's 2018 application to exceed Pacific Power's large-load direct-access cap and its 2019 withdrawal; UE 374 Order 21-090 records Vitesse participation concerning Schedule 272. Neither discloses campus kWh, demand, bill or substation cost. OWRD WRIS at https://apps.wrd.state.or.us/apps/wr/wrinfo/ and the 2019 Prineville ASR application/2020 attachment were searched for Vitesse, Facebook, Meta, 735 Connect Way, CROO 53878, G-17089 and G-17236; City rights and ASR permitting appear, but no Vitesse-specific right or annual meter/bill allocation. DEQ's current Your DEQ Online route and pre-November-2024 archive were searched for Vitesse, Facebook, Meta, Prineville and 735 Connect Way; no exact facility air permit or generator inventory surfaced, and the Tier 4 permit is a generic template. EPA facility searches likewise produced no exact campus generator/emissions record. Eight electricity observations remain direct; Meta's rounded 328-megaliter 2024 withdrawal remains only as the single disclosed unit conversion. No tariff assignment, peak demand, IT load, water bill, consumption/discharge, current right allocation, project-funded utility cost, generator count or facility emissions value was found.

source.title: Meta 2025 Environmental Data Index
source.notes: Facility tables report Forest City electricity consumption of 535,555 MWh, water withdrawal of 16 megaliters, zero market-based Scope 2 emissions and 144,104 metric tons CO2e of location-based Scope 2 emissions for 2024. research_updates.notes: Meta Community Action Grant pages, Crook County School District board/site search, ORTOP, OSU-Cascades, NeighborImpact, Crook County Kids, Bowman Museum, CASA, libraries and named recipients were searched for 2011-2026 using Facebook, Meta, Prineville, grant, gift, robotics, STEM, nonprofit, school and volunteer. No complete annual campus grant ledger, payment date, in-kind valuation, volunteer-hour value or Crook-only allocation for regional programs was found.

source.title: Our Prineville Data Center is growing again!
source.notes: Operator announcement describes a planned 900,000-square-foot, two-building expansion that would produce an 11-building, nearly 4.6-million-square-foot campus and more than $2 billion of investment at completion. It also announces a $60,000 Crook County School District robotics grant and says total Facebook support for the program had reached $150,000. The future-completion values are projections; the two community figures overlap.

research_updates.title: Structured-data and modeling audit — county comparison gaps removed; one conversion retained
research_updates.notes: All four prior syntheses were reassessed against the expanded direct register. The three inverse-distance-weighted county GDP, employment and wage gaps were removed: each is noncausal, the 2011 anchor is followed by multiple Meta phases and Apple's separate campus, and the results add no defensible decision value beyond observed county series; the employment fit was especially poor. The only retained synthesis converts Meta's rounded 328-megaliter 2024 Prineville facility withdrawal to gallons with an explicit rounding band because the direct register lacks a compatible annual-water-withdrawal metric. No supplier, construction-employment, payroll, induced-spending, net-fiscal or public-service-cost model is eligible without local-purchase shares, project payroll, recipient alignment and same-scope cost inputs. The newly direct annual LRZ tax-savings series is not modeled. No records requests were made.

project_description: Meta's Prineville Data Center is a Meta-operated campus at 735 Connect Way in Prineville, Crook County, Oregon, not a single building or statewide portfolio. Facebook broke ground in 2010 and launched the first dedicated facility in 2011; City records identify the original 119.5-acre parcel, while contractor records describe two early 300,000-square-foot data halls and a 70,000-square-foot administration building. A March 2021 operator announcement described two planned additions that would bring the campus to 11 buildings and nearly 4.6 million square feet, so those expansion dimensions and the associated investment forecast are kept separate from the original facility.
